name: Remote Lead
tagline: Manage people you never see in the office
about: Remote Lead is a toolkit for managers of distributed teams: make work visible without surveillance, run hybrid meetings that don't sideline remote people, catch quiet disengagement from written signals, and write the team working agreement that sets core hours, response times and camera rules.
persona: You are a coach for remote managers: high trust, high clarity, allergic to surveillance; you build systems that make good work visible instead of hours online.

onboarding.title: Lead well from a distance
onboarding.subtitle: A little about your team shapes every template.

tools.title: Make work visible
tools.subtitle: See progress without watching people

inputs.label: What you can't see
inputs.placeholder: who's overloaded, whether the roadmap is on track, who's blocked

tools.prompt: The manager can't see: {worry}, and will accept '{overhead}' of reporting overhead per person. Produce a table (Signal you want | Lightweight source | Cadence | Minutes per person) with at least 5 rows using written check-ins, demos, boards and existing artefacts rather than tracking tools, a quote with a weekly written check-in template of 3–5 questions people can answer in under 10 minutes, steps to roll it out over 3 weeks for the profile team, and a callout on why monitoring software costs more trust than it buys.

tools.title: Hybrid meeting rules
tools.subtitle: Stop sidelining the remote half

inputs.label: What's going wrong
inputs.placeholder: remote people can't hear, decisions get made in the office after the call

tools.prompt: Team mix: '{mix}'. Symptoms: {symptoms}. Produce a table (Practice | Rule | Who enforces it | Fixes which symptom) with at least 6 rules such as one-remote-all-remote, shared notes, hand-raise order and decisions recorded in writing, a quote with the meeting protocol to post in the team channel, a checklist for the host to run 5 minutes before any hybrid meeting, and a callout on proximity bias in visibility and promotions and how to counter it for the profile team.

tools.title: Quiet signals
tools.subtitle: Spot someone struggling from text

inputs.label: What you've noticed
inputs.placeholder: Sam's PRs dropped from 6 to 1 a week, camera off, one-word replies since the reorg

tools.prompt: Observations about {person}: {observations}. Produce a table (Signal | Benign explanation | Concerning explanation | How to check gently), a text section with your read of the most likely situation and how confident you are, a quote with a low-pressure 1:1 opener that names the pattern without accusing, and a callout on what a manager should never do here (monitoring tools, public call-outs) and when to involve HR or wellbeing support.

tools.title: Team working agreement
tools.subtitle: Core hours, response times, camera rules

inputs.label: What keeps going wrong
inputs.placeholder: people expect instant Slack replies, 7am calls for the Polish folks, cameras-off arguments

tools.prompt: Draft a working agreement for the profile team, whose work is mostly '{urgency}', to fix: {friction}. Produce a kv (core overlap hours shown in every profile time zone, expected reply time per channel, camera policy, meeting-free blocks, how to flag urgent, where decisions are recorded), a table (Norm | The rule | Example | Allowed exception) with at least 8 rows, a quote with the agreement post ready to pin in the team channel under 250 words, and steps for ratifying it with the team and revisiting it in 6 weeks.

tools.title: Remote first week
tools.subtitle: A new hire's week, hour by hour

inputs.label: New hire & role
inputs.placeholder: Lena, frontend dev, starts Monday in Berlin

tools.prompt: Plan the first week for {hire} with buddy and key people: {buddy}. Sections: a table (Day | Morning | Afternoon | Who they meet | Goal) for 5 days respecting the profile time zones, a checklist for the manager before day one (accounts, hardware, first ticket, intro post), a quote with the welcome message to post to the team, and a callout on the isolation risk in weeks 2–4 and the single ritual that reduces it.

disclaimer: Management guidance, not HR, legal or mental-health advice; follow your company's policies and involve HR for formal matters or wellbeing concerns.
